pathways.title: Alkene Hydrogenation
pathways.shortExplanation: Hydrogenation adds H₂ across the C=C bond, reducing the alkene to an alkane.

pathways.title: Catalytic Deuteration
pathways.shortExplanation: Catalytic deuteration adds one explicit deuterium (D) to each alkene carbon. PocketChem keeps the isotope atoms in the product structure so the D labels can be drawn.
selectivity: D and D add to the same face of the alkene (syn addition).

pathways.title: HX Addition: Hydrobromination
pathways.shortExplanation: Under ordinary ionic conditions, HBr protonates the alkene and bromide attacks the more stable carbocation. For an unsymmetrical alkene this normally places Br on the more substituted carbon.
selectivity: For an unsymmetrical alkene, Br is normally placed on the more substituted carbon (Markovnikov orientation).
Carbocation rearrangements can occur under the ionic mechanism.
limitations: When the first-formed carbocation can shift to a clearly more stable one (3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene) both the direct and the rearranged halide are listed and neither is ranked: textbooks report an approximately equal mixture for HCl + 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene. Shifts between equally stable cations are not generated.

pathways.title: HX Addition: Hydrochlorination
pathways.shortExplanation: Under ordinary ionic conditions, HCl protonates the alkene and chloride attacks the more stable carbocation. For an unsymmetrical alkene this normally places Cl on the more substituted carbon.
selectivity: For an unsymmetrical alkene, Cl is normally placed on the more substituted carbon (Markovnikov orientation).
Carbocation rearrangements can occur under the ionic mechanism.
limitations: When the first-formed carbocation can shift to a clearly more stable one (3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene) both the direct and the rearranged halide are listed and neither is ranked: textbooks report an approximately equal mixture for HCl + 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene. Shifts between equally stable cations are not generated.

pathways.title: HX Addition: Hydroiodination
pathways.shortExplanation: Under ordinary ionic conditions, HI protonates the alkene and iodide attacks the more stable carbocation. For an unsymmetrical alkene this normally places I on the more substituted carbon.
selectivity: For an unsymmetrical alkene, I is normally placed on the more substituted carbon (Markovnikov orientation).
Carbocation rearrangements can occur under the ionic mechanism.
limitations: When the first-formed carbocation can shift to a clearly more stable one (3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene) both the direct and the rearranged halide are listed and neither is ranked: textbooks report an approximately equal mixture for HCl + 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene. Shifts between equally stable cations are not generated.

pathways.title: Hydrobromination (Peroxide Effect)
pathways.shortExplanation: In the presence of peroxides, HBr adds by a radical-chain mechanism and gives the anti-Markovnikov constitutional product.
selectivity: Br goes to the less substituted alkene carbon (anti-Markovnikov).

pathways.title: Halogenation
pathways.shortExplanation: Halogenation adds one bromine to each alkene carbon.
selectivity: Anti addition
More substituted/electron-rich alkene sites are preferred when several nonequivalent C=C bonds are present.

pathways.title: Halohydrin Formation
pathways.reagentNote: Anti addition of Br and OH
pathways.shortExplanation: The alkene forms a bromonium ion, then water attacks the more substituted carbon. The result is a vicinal bromohydrin with OH on the more substituted carbon and Br on the less substituted carbon.
selectivity: OH goes to the more substituted alkene carbon and Br to the less substituted carbon.
Br and OH add anti through bromonium-ion opening.
limitations: The anti relationship is applied for 1,2-disubstituted alkenes drawn as E or Z and for alkenes in 5-7 membered rings. A chiral product of an achiral reaction is shown as both enantiomers (a racemate); an acyclic alkene of undefined geometry, or a tri-/tetrasubstituted one, is left without assigned stereochemistry.

pathways.title: Acid-Catalyzed Hydration
pathways.reagentLabel: H₂O/H⁺ (e.g. H₂O + dilute H₂SO₄ or H₃PO₄)
pathways.shortExplanation: Water adds across the alkene under acidic conditions. For an unsymmetrical alkene, protonation favors the more stable carbocation, so OH normally ends up on the more substituted carbon.
selectivity: For an unsymmetrical alkene, OH normally forms on the more substituted carbon (Markovnikov orientation).
Carbocation rearrangements may occur.
limitations: When the first-formed carbocation can shift to a clearly more stable one (3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene) both the direct and the rearranged alcohol are listed and neither is ranked. Shifts between equally stable cations are not generated.

pathways.title: Hydroboration-Oxidation
pathways.shortExplanation: Hydroboration-oxidation hydrates the alkene with anti-Markovnikov orientation.
selectivity: Anti-Markovnikov and syn addition
limitations: The current hydration handler enforces anti-Markovnikov connectivity; syn stereochemistry is not yet assigned explicitly in the product structure.

pathways.title: Oxymercuration-Demercuration
pathways.shortExplanation: Oxymercuration-demercuration converts an alkene to a Markovnikov alcohol without rearrangement.
selectivity: Markovnikov orientation without rearrangement

pathways.title: Simmons–Smith Cyclopropanation
pathways.shortExplanation: A methylene carbenoid adds across the double bond to form a cyclopropane while preserving the alkene's relative stereochemistry.
selectivity: Stereospecific cyclopropanation; alkene geometry is retained in the ring relationship.

pathways.title: Dichlorocyclopropanation
pathways.shortExplanation: Base generates dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) from chloroform. The carbene adds across the alkene to form a cyclopropane bearing two chlorines on the newly inserted carbon.
selectivity: Carbene addition is stereospecific and preserves the alkene's relative stereochemistry.

pathways.title: Dibromocyclopropanation
pathways.shortExplanation: Base generates dibromocarbene (:CBr₂) from bromoform. The carbene adds across the alkene to form a cyclopropane bearing two bromines on the newly inserted carbon.
selectivity: Carbene addition is stereospecific and preserves the alkene's relative stereochemistry.

pathways.title: Epoxidation
pathways.shortExplanation: A peroxyacid converts the alkene into a three-membered epoxide ring.
selectivity: Stereospecific oxygen transfer
When several nonequivalent isolated alkenes are present, the more substituted/electron-rich alkene is preferred; exact ties remain as alternatives.

pathways.title: Syn Dihydroxylation
pathways.reagentNote: Syn addition of two OH groups
pathways.shortExplanation: Syn dihydroxylation adds two hydroxyl groups to the same face of the alkene. Common reagent systems are OsO₄ with H₂O₂, OsO₄ with NMO, or cold dilute basic KMnO₄.
selectivity: Both OH groups add to the same face of the alkene (syn addition).

pathways.title: Anti Dihydroxylation
pathways.shortExplanation: Epoxidation followed by acid-catalyzed ring opening gives an anti vicinal diol.
selectivity: The two OH groups end up on opposite faces (anti addition).

pathways.title: Reductive Ozonolysis
pathways.shortExplanation: Ozone cleaves the alkene. Dimethyl sulfide or zinc prevents further oxidation, giving aldehydes and ketones.

pathways.title: Oxidative Ozonolysis
pathways.shortExplanation: Oxidative workup converts any aldehydes formed during ozonolysis into carboxylic acids while ketones remain ketones.
pathways.productLabel: nonanoic acid (pelargonic acid) + Name not available (unsupported structure)

pathways.title: Hot Permanganate Oxidative Cleavage
pathways.shortExplanation: Hot permanganate cleaves the alkene. An alkene carbon with no hydrogen gives a ketone, one bearing a hydrogen gives a carboxylic acid, and a terminal CH₂ carbon is oxidized to CO₂.
pathways.productLabel: nonanoic acid (pelargonic acid) + Name not available (unsupported structure)

pathways.title: Allylic Bromination
pathways.reagentNote: Radical substitution at an allylic carbon
pathways.shortExplanation: NBS replaces an allylic hydrogen with bromine while minimizing direct addition of Br₂ across the double bond.
selectivity: Reaction occurs at an allylic C–H bond.
limitations: Resonance-related allylic bromides can form; the engine enumerates local sites but does not rank the product mixture.

pathways.title: Addition Polymerization
pathways.reagentLabel: radical, cationic, anionic, or coordination initiator
pathways.shortExplanation: Many alkenes undergo chain-growth addition polymerization in which the pi bond becomes part of a saturated polymer backbone.
limitations: A polymer requires repeat-unit, tacticity, end-group, and chain-length representation rather than a finite small-molecule SMILES product.

pathways.title: Haloether Formation
pathways.reagentNote: Anti addition of Br and OR
pathways.shortExplanation: An alcohol opens the bromonium ion formed from the alkene. The alcohol's OR group bonds to the more substituted alkene carbon while Br remains on the less substituted carbon, giving a haloether.
selectivity: OR goes to the more substituted alkene carbon and Br to the less substituted carbon.
Br and OR add anti through bromonium-ion opening.
limitations: The supplied alcohol's actual R group is carried into the ether. Explicit anti stereocenter assignment will be completed in the alkene stereochemistry phase.
Draw the additional reactant in the same Ketcher canvas: alcohol (ROH).

pathways.title: Alkoxymercuration-Demercuration
pathways.shortExplanation: Alkoxymercuration-demercuration adds OR and H across an alkene. The oxygen of the supplied alcohol becomes bonded to the more substituted alkene carbon, giving a Markovnikov ether without a free carbocation rearrangement.
selectivity: OR goes to the more substituted alkene carbon (Markovnikov orientation).
No carbocation rearrangement is expected.
limitations: Draw the additional reactant in the same Ketcher canvas: alcohol (ROH).

pathways.title: Epoxidation Followed by Acidic Alcohol Opening
pathways.reagentNote: Draw the alkene and the alcohol nucleophile as disconnected structures
pathways.shortExplanation: The alkene is first converted stereospecifically to an epoxide. Under acidic conditions a drawn alcohol opens the protonated epoxide by backside attack at the more substituted epoxide carbon, installing that alcohol's OR group anti to the oxygen-derived OH.
selectivity: Epoxidation preserves the alkene's relative stereochemistry.
Acidic epoxide opening is backside/anti.
Acidic opening favors attack at the more substituted epoxide carbon; equal-substitution cases remain genuine alternatives.
The OR group is taken from the alcohol actually drawn by the user; methanol therefore gives OMe, ethanol gives OEt, and so on.
limitations: Draw the additional reactant in the same Ketcher canvas: alcohol nucleophile (ROH).

pathways.title: Epoxidation Followed by Grignard/Organolithium Opening
pathways.reagentLabel: 1) 1 equiv mCPBA or RCO₃H  2) RMgX or RLi  3) H₃O⁺
pathways.shortExplanation: One equivalent of peroxyacid converts one alkene into an epoxide. A drawn Grignard or organolithium reagent then opens that epoxide at the less substituted carbon; acidic workup gives the alcohol.
selectivity: One equivalent of mCPBA gives monoepoxidation rather than epoxidizing every C=C bond.
Among nonequivalent isolated alkenes, the more substituted/electron-rich alkene is preferred; exact site-selectivity ties are retained.

RMgX/RLi attacks the less substituted epoxide carbon by backside opening, so the new C–C bond and OH are anti; one wedge/dash representative is drawn rather than duplicating its mirror image as another regioisomer.
limitations: When two alkene sites have indistinguishable substitution/electronic ranking, both genuinely competitive sites are retained instead of choosing one arbitrarily.
Draw the additional reactant in the same Ketcher canvas: Grignard or organolithium reagent.
pathways.productLabel: Alcohol with a new C–C bond

pathways.title: Photochemical Alkene–Alkyne [2+2] Cycloaddition
pathways.reagentNote: Photochemical [2+2] between an alkene and an alkyne
pathways.shortExplanation: An alkene and an alkyne can undergo a photochemical [2+2] cycloaddition. One alkyne π bond and the alkene π bond form two new C–C σ bonds, leaving a cyclobutene double bond.
selectivity: This is a photochemical [2+2], not a Diels–Alder [4+2] reaction.
limitations: Unsymmetrical alkene/alkyne pairs can have genuine regioselectivity that depends on substituent electronics and is not universally captured by one generic rule.
Draw the additional reactant in the same Ketcher canvas: alkyne reaction partner.

pathways.title: Photochemical [2+2] Cycloaddition
pathways.shortExplanation: Under photochemical excitation, two alkene π bonds can undergo a [2+2] cycloaddition. Each C=C becomes a single bond and two new C–C bonds form between the alkene termini, creating a four-membered cyclobutane ring.
selectivity: Consumes one alkene from each drawn reactant and forms a cyclobutane ring.
When several C=C atom-map embeddings are possible, PocketChem displays one representative major [2+2] product instead of enumerating every mapping-derived alternative.
limitations: This rule models intermolecular [2+2] cycloaddition between two disconnected alkene-containing structures.

If a substrate is known experimentally to give a genuine regioisomeric mixture, a dedicated substrate-specific rule should declare that mixture explicitly rather than relying on generic atom-map enumeration.
Ordinary thermal alkene [2+2] cycloaddition is not represented by this rule; hν is required.
Draw the additional reactant in the same Ketcher canvas: alkene reaction partner.
pathways.productLabel: Cyclobutane formed from the two alkene π bonds

selected.title: Hydroboration-Oxidation
selected.shortExplanation: Hydroboration-oxidation hydrates the alkene with anti-Markovnikov orientation.
selectivity: Anti-Markovnikov and syn addition
limitations: The current hydration handler enforces anti-Markovnikov connectivity; syn stereochemistry is not yet assigned explicitly in the product structure.

interfaceLimitation: Conditions are represented by fixed pathway-family filters and explicit nucleophile/base molecules; engine listing API accepts no solvent/temperature field. No target-dependent fallback.
